description: The idempotency fix for iter-2 FIND-007 (decide.py:50-64, _already_traded_window) dedupes on the tuple (window_end_ms, side), not on window_end_ms alone. Because decide.py's cron pass is documented in SKILL.md:26 as running 'every ~1 min during a window,' and momentum.side_and_prob's chosen side can flip within a single 5-min window as BTC spot price oscillates (momentum.py:31-42, purely a function of the return-so-far at call time), it is possible for the SAME window to first produce an 'UP' paper trade on one wake and a 'DOWN' paper trade on a later wake within the same window -- the dedup key (window_end_ms='UP') and (window_end_ms='DOWN') are treated as distinct and both are allowed to be recorded. This means a single underlying 5-min event can generate two conflicting paper positions, both of which resolve.py will independently resolve and gate.py will independently count toward the win-rate/net statistics -- inflating the effective sample size and mixing two contradictory bets into what the operator/SKILL.md documentation implies is one signal per window. This is a residual, real gap in the idempotency fix, not a full re-opening of FIND-007 (exact-duplicate spam is genuinely blocked) but a documented-behavior mismatch that should be tracked.

evidence.snippet: if r.get("src") == "momentum" and r.get("window_end_ms") == window_end_ms and r.get("side") == side: return True  -- keyed on (window_end_ms, side), so a same-window side flip is not deduped
